text.p: Base metal activity remained slow during Monday afternoon LME trading, with markets trapped in unexciting ranges, traders said.
In Chicago, the Commodites Research Bureau Index added 0.21 points to 246.81.

LME copper business was confined to an extremely tight $11 band, with the market showing little enthusiasm for tackling the $2,500 level overhead. The spread backwardation did widen slightly, which maintained a steady undertone. By the end of the kerb three months prices were at $2,488, up just $1 a tonne from last Friday's kerb close. In the short-term, jobber activity will predominate between $2,475 and $2,500, traders say.

Aluminium displayed a steadier sheen after some early forward buying flipped the market above $1,600, although the upmove ran into a buffer of resistance around $1,690. Last trade was at $1,603, up $6.

Nickel's performance was lacklustre and after aimlessly ranging around $7,300 for most of the session prices tailed away during the kerb. The market closed at $7,250, down $60, and continue to wait for developments at the strike-bound Inco Sudbury facility.
Zinc lost ground during the day, staging a mini-correction to Friday's advances to fresh 4-1/2 year highs, and final trade was $11 easier at $1,356.

The tin market was less heated on the spread front, as the contango reverted back to around $45/45 after touching $14 last Friday. This defused a rally in forward values, with three months closing at $5,580, down $130.
Lead was confined to a $4 band, and closed at $641, down just $1. Alloy ended at a stable $1,472/75.

CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed higher on rain delayed harvest in Texas and Oklahoma plus fund short covering, traders said. "Funds were buying back their shorts," said Charlie Sernatinger, analyst for E.D. and F. Man International. "They (harvest crews) harvested up until about noon Sunday with excellent quality. But they (commercials and elevators) did buy a lot of wheat at up eight cents today." Wheat closed five to nine cents per bushel higher, with July up eight at $3.67-1/2.

COMEX and NYMEX precious metals ended mixed Monday, after giving back the session's early gains, on light volumes. "Gold found some support as the dollar slipped further, but silver saw some fund and bullion bank selling, and platinum and palladium both saw some light profit taking, but volumes were very thin," North American Equity Services floor trader John Geraghty said. COMEX August gold ended up 60 cents at $346.30 an ounce, but ended off the session highs at $347.30 on very low volumes. In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $344.00/50 an ounce, compared to the London Monday afternoon fix at $344.25 and the New York close Friday around $343.20/70.

IPE Brent crude futures failed to recover from last week's heavy losses on Monday, and fell rapidly in late trade to close at the session low. July Brent closed 16 cents down at $17.54 a barrel -- the yearly spot low on the continuation chart -- having shed 62 cents in Friday's session. "We had a couple of pushes to the upside but this market just isn't ready for it," said one broker.
